title: Shortcut tests must traverse real event bindings
environment: Observed Windows/Tk application path. Synthetic event success does not establish every physical keyboard, widget or focus configuration.
goal: Verify a press/release recording shortcut after interacting with UI controls.
approach: Historical failed assumption: Testing the handler function was assumed to test keyboard dispatch.
what_worked: Historical correction: Install a first-priority recording bindtag on relevant widgets while exempting text entry; change self-tests to generated KeyPress/KeyRelease events. Verification reported by the source: Three press-to-start/release-to-stop cycles traversed the binding path and ended with idle state, without dropped or padded frames.
what_failed: Historical observed failure: A direct recording-function self-test passed, but the shortcut failed when focused widgets consumed the key in class bindings.
why: Confirmed: root-window-only bindings ran too late for the affected focus paths.
improved_method: Test the entry event with realistic focus, not just its callback. Preserve typing and modifier behavior when changing shortcut precedence.
when_to_use: Observed Windows/Tk application path. Synthetic event success does not establish every physical keyboard, widget or focus configuration.
when_not_to_use: Synthetic event success does not establish every physical keyboard, widget or focus configuration.
known_limitations: This is an independently curated generalization of an earlier recorded failure. No source-side experiment was rerun during this registration; observation_date is the 2026-10-09 knowledge-review date, not the incident date. Applicability and root-cause claims remain limited to the source-reported conditions.
